headline: Test 2: Virginia, 1640–1705 · 46:01

items.title: 46:01 · Step two arrived in December 1662 when
items.detail: Step two arrived in December 1662, when the Virginia House of Burgesses enacted the hereditary slave statute of partus sequitur ventrem.

items.title: 46:09 · That 1662 statute decreed that all children
items.detail: That 1662 statute decreed that all children born in the colony would be held bond or free solely according to the legal condition of the mother.

items.title: 46:20 · By reversing several centuries of English common-law
items.detail: By reversing several centuries of English common-law paternity rules, the 1662 statute converted the reproductive capacity of enslaved Black women into a self-replenishing capital asset and insulated white planters who fathered children with enslaved women.

items.title: 46:34 · In 1664 neighboring Maryland enacted its lifelong
items.detail: In 1664, neighboring Maryland enacted its lifelong servitude statute, and in October 1669 Virginia passed An Act About the Casual Killing of Slaves.
